html:
Private notes written in Greek by the emperor Marcus Aurelius, probably between about 170 and his death in 180. Their Greek title means "to himself"; they were reminders, not a book for readers.

Much of it was written in army camps during the Marcomannic Wars. One section is headed "among the Quadi", another "at Carnuntum". The notes are short and often repeat the same few ideas from Stoicism, which Marcus learned largely from Epictetus:

  • Only your own judgments are in your power; things outside you cannot harm your character.
  • Do your duty to the common good, since all people share in reason.
  • Everything passes quickly, fame included.

The first book is a list of thanks to the people who taught him. The text survived in a few manuscripts and was first printed in 1559. It has since become one of the most read works of ancient philosophy.
sum: Private notes written in Greek by the emperor Marcus Aurelius, probably between about 170 and his death in 180. Their Greek title means "to himself"; they were reminders, not a book for readers.
